Title: Adverse events in different administration routes of semaglutide: a pharmacovigilance study based on FAERS
Research_Objective: Compare ADR profiles across semaglutide administration routes
Methodology: FAERS disproportionality analysis (ROR) comparing oral vs subcutaneous semaglutide
Major_Findings: Different ADR profiles identified for oral vs subcutaneous routes; GI events more common with oral
Limitations: FAERS limitations (voluntary reporting; no denominator); potential reporting bias
Relevance: Directly relevant - establishes baseline ADR landscape for semaglutide using FAERS
Research_Gap: Route-specific psychiatric ADR analysis not performed

Title: Comparative analysis of semaglutide induced adverse reactions: FAERS database and social media reviews
Research_Objective: Compare FAERS and social media ADR reporting for semaglutide
Methodology: FAERS disproportionality analysis + social media text mining
Major_Findings: Social media captures patient-reported ADRs not well represented in FAERS; complementary data sources
Limitations: Social media data quality; selection bias; FAERS voluntary reporting
Relevance: Demonstrates need for multi-source pharmacovigilance approaches
Research_Gap: Integration of social media with FAERS for psychiatric signal detection unexplored

Title: A real-world disproportionality analysis of semaglutide: Post-marketing pharmacovigilance data
Research_Objective: Comprehensive disproportionality analysis of semaglutide in FAERS
Methodology: ROR and PRR analysis across multiple ADR categories
Major_Findings: Multiple disproportionate signals identified across organ systems
Limitations: FAERS inherent limitations; confounding by indication
Relevance: Core reference for disproportionality methodology applied to semaglutide
Research_Gap: Psychiatric ADR category requires deeper comparative analysis

Title: Semaglutide: NAION in FAERS - A disproportionality analysis
Methodology: FAERS disproportionality analysis for ophthalmic events
Major_Findings: Significant disproportionate signal for NAION with semaglutide
Limitations: FAERS limitations; small absolute numbers; confounding
Relevance: Demonstrates FAERS detecting novel signals not identified in RCTs
Research_Gap: Cross-system ADR comparison (ophthalmic vs psychiatric) needed

Title: Mortality and SAEs Associated with GLP-1 RAs: FAERS Pharmacovigilance Study
Research_Objective: Evaluate mortality and SAE patterns for GLP-1 RAs in FAERS
Methodology: FAERS analysis of serious outcomes including death
Major_Findings: Identified patterns of serious adverse events and mortality reports
Limitations: FAERS limitations; no causation; reporting bias
Relevance: Provides context for severity of ADR signals
Research_Gap: Psychiatric ADR severity (suicidality outcomes) needs specific analysis

Title: Depression and suicide/self-injury signals for weight loss medications: FAERS disproportionality analysis
Research_Objective: Analyze depression/suicidality signals for semaglutide liraglutide tirzepatide
Methodology: FAERS disproportionality analysis with multiple GLP-1 RA comparison
Major_Findings: Depression and suicidality signals identified; differences across GLP-1 RAs
Limitations: FAERS limitations; confounding by comorbid depression; Weber effect
Relevance: Most directly relevant - psychiatric ADR signal detection for the target drug
Research_Gap: Active comparator (SGLT2i) analysis for psychiatric ADRs not performed

Title: READUS-PV: Reporting of Disproportionality Analysis for Drug Safety Signal Detection
Research_Objective: Develop standardized reporting checklist for disproportionality analyses
Major_Findings: 14-item reporting checklist (READUS-PV) for transparent disproportionality analyses
Limitations: Checklist compliance voluntary; may not capture all quality dimensions
Relevance: Provides methodological framework for this project's FAERS analysis
Research_Gap: Checklist application to psychiatric ADR-specific analyses not demonstrated

Title: Once-Weekly Semaglutide in Adults with Overweight or Obesity (STEP 1)
Major_Findings: 14.9% mean weight reduction; primarily GI adverse events; high completion rate
Limitations: Industry-sponsored; psychiatric exclusions; short duration; no active comparator
Relevance: Baseline controlled trial data for comparison with FAERS findings
Research_Gap: Psychiatric ADR monitoring limited by exclusion criteria and sample size

Title: WHO Data on Semaglutide Liraglutide and Suicidality
Research_Objective: Analyze suicidality signals for GLP-1 RAs in WHO VigiBase
Major_Findings: Suicidal ideation signal for semaglutide especially with antidepressant co-prescription
Limitations: VigiBase limitations similar to FAERS; confounding; observational
Relevance: Corroborates FAERS psychiatric signals using independent database
Research_Gap: Need for prospective validation; antidepressant interaction mechanism unclear

Title: GLP-1 RAs and suicidality: reports to FAERS
Research_Objective: Evaluate GLP-1 RA suicidality signals in FAERS
Methodology: FAERS disproportionality analysis with causality assessment framework
Major_Findings: Disproportionate suicidal ideation reporting but no causal link by Bradford Hill criteria
Limitations: FAERS limitations; Bradford Hill criteria cannot definitively exclude causation
Relevance: Critical nuanced analysis distinguishing signal from causation
Research_Gap: Prospective studies needed to resolve causation question

Title: Semaglutide and suicidal ideation risk in real-world cohort
Research_Objective: Assess semaglutide-suicidal ideation association using EHR data
Methodology: EHR-based cohort analysis with propensity score matching
Major_Findings: Semaglutide associated with LOWER risk of suicidal ideation (contradicts FAERS)
Limitations: Observational; residual confounding; EHR coding limitations
Relevance: Key contradictory finding - challenges FAERS psychiatric signal interpretation
Research_Gap: Reconciliation of FAERS signal vs protective EHR finding needed

Title: GI Safety of GLP-1 RAs in US: FAERS Analysis
Research_Objective: Assess GI safety profile of GLP-1 RAs
Methodology: FAERS analysis of GI adverse events (16000+ reports)
Major_Findings: Strong GI ADR association (nausea vomiting delayed gastric emptying)
Limitations: FAERS limitations; GI events well known
Relevance: Provides GI ADR context for comparison with psychiatric signals
Research_Gap: Psychiatric vs GI ADR comparative severity analysis lacking

Title: Anti-obesity medications and digestive adverse events: FAERS study
Research_Objective: Stratified analysis of digestive ADEs for anti-obesity drugs
Methodology: FAERS stratified analysis comparing semaglutide and liraglutide
Major_Findings: Semaglutide/liraglutide correlation with GI events; pancreatitis signals
Limitations: FAERS limitations; stratification may reduce power
Relevance: Methodological reference for stratified FAERS analysis approach
Research_Gap: Cross-system stratified analysis (GI + psychiatric) not performed

Title: GLP-1 RA metabolic and nutritional adverse events
Research_Objective: Evaluate metabolic/nutritional safety of GLP-1 RAs
Methodology: FAERS analysis of metabolic adverse events
Major_Findings: Metabolic safety signatures including dehydration and hypoglycemia profiles
Limitations: FAERS limitations; metabolic confounding with weight loss
Relevance: Broadens ADR profile understanding beyond GI and psychiatric
Research_Gap: Metabolic ADR interaction with psychiatric outcomes unexplored

Title: Ophthalmic ADRs with GLP-1 RAs: FAERS pharmacovigilance
Research_Objective: Evaluate ophthalmic ADR risk with GLP-1 RAs
Methodology: FAERS disproportionality analysis for ophthalmic events (5000+ reports)
Major_Findings: Significant ophthalmic ADR signals including retinopathy and visual impairment
Limitations: FAERS limitations; confounding by diabetes (diabetic retinopathy)
Relevance: Cross-system ADR detection capability of FAERS
Research_Gap: Multi-system ADR profiling (ophthalmic + psychiatric) in single analysis needed

Title: Alopecia with semaglutide and tirzepatide: FAERS disproportionality
Research_Objective: Evaluate alopecia signal for semaglutide/tirzepatide in FAERS
Major_Findings: Statistically significant alopecia signal for both drugs
Limitations: Short time window; confounding with weight loss; FAERS limitations
Relevance: Novel ADR identification demonstrating FAERS value for emerging signals
Research_Gap: Weight-loss-mediated vs drug-mediated ADR mechanism unclear

Title: Alopecia with GLP-1 RAs: Scoping Review
Research_Objective: Review alopecia evidence associated with GLP-1 RAs
Methodology: Systematic literature review with case report analysis
Major_Findings: Corroborates FAERS alopecia signal with clinical case evidence
Limitations: Scoping review limitations; small case numbers
